Build a Crop-Rotation Alluvial (Sankey) Plot Efficiently

Source: R/functions.R
build_sankey_plot.Rd

Builds the same stratum/flow ggalluvial visualization as passing a full one-row-per-(id, year) table straight into geom_flow()/geom_stratum(), but aggregates each adjacent year-pair by (source crop, target crop) first. ggalluvial's stat_flow() (used by geom_flow()) only ever matches rows within one adjacent pair of x positions - it does not need full multi-year alluvium identity - so summing same-transition rows before plotting produces identical stratum heights and flow widths while collapsing the input from one row per unique rotation sequence (potentially hundreds of thousands) down to at most (number of distinct crops)^2 rows per year-pair. This is what makes the Sankey tab slow to render at real-world data scale: the underlying geometry was always small, but ggalluvial had to grind through the full, un-aggregated row count to discover that.

Each year-pair gets its own geom_flow() layer (rather than one layer fed all pairs at once): if a single layer's data spans more than one adjacent pair, stat_flow() cannot tell that a row's alluvium id is only meant to link within its own pair, and it inserts an extra "unmatched remainder" flow at interior years - silently doubling the apparent flow at every year that isn't the first or last. Keeping each pair's aggregated rows in an isolated layer avoids this entirely.

build_sankey_plot(rotation_long, crop_colors, text_size = 15, dark = TRUE)

Arguments

rotation_long

data.frame/data.table with columns Area, id, key, year (one row per entity per year; Area constant across a given id's rows), as produced by transform_rotation_data()[[1]].

crop_colors

Named character vector mapping crop names to hex colors.

text_size

Numeric text size for stratum labels/theme.

dark

Logical, dark theme flag passed to sankey_plot_theme().

Value

A ggplot object. Callers still add their own guides() call to set the legend row count, exactly as before.
